ev.q: Among 987 persons screened, 145 (14.7%) had splenomegaly and received further testing.
Specimens from five (3.5%) patients were positive for hepatitis B surface antigen
There was some evidence of family clustering, with 33 (22.7%) of the 145 cases occurring in families.
During two evaluations of refugee populations in western Uganda in March and July 2015
Among the 145 patients with splenomegaly, 63.4% were aged 5–17 years (median = 14.8 years).

methods_quotes.q: defined as >4 standard deviations above the local mean for splenic size, adjusted for height, based on the World Health Organization ultrasonography protocol
thin blood smear tests performed for all 145 cases were negative (thick films were not performed)
